title: Origins: Molecules That Copy Themselves
description: A reaction whose product speeds up its own making grows exponentially and can oscillate, flare and spread as a wave. A prion does it with shape alone: a misfolded protein that refolds the healthy ones it touches. Unlocks Autocatalytic Broth and the Prion Lattice.

puzzle.goal: Two reagents A and B are fed in at constant concentration. A makes an intermediate X; B turns X into Y; X decays; and - the autocatalytic step - two X and one Y make three X, so X catalyses its own production. In dimensionless units with every rate constant 1, write how fast X changes.
puzzle.name: Brusselator (autocatalytic chemical oscillator), the X equation
puzzle.ask: The steady state is X = A, Y = B/A. It loses stability - and the mixture starts to oscillate on its own, a chemical clock - once B exceeds 1 + A². Find that critical B for the A below.

vars.A: feed concentration of the first reagent
vars.B: feed concentration of the second reagent

puzzle.method: Add up the four steps: A → X adds A, B + X → Y removes BX, X → product removes X, 2X + Y → 3X adds X²Y.
